 Shri Vinayak Balchandani, learned counsel for the pet  Dr. Amit Bhatia, learned Govt. Advocate for the respo  ORDER 1.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
By this petition preferred under Article 226 of the Constitution of India the petitioner has challenged the notice dated 27.06.2025 (Annexure P/1) issued by the Additional District Magistrate,
District Indore whereby he has been directed to submit his reply through the authorized officer of the company.
2. On 11.09.2024 respondent No.1 raided a firm in the name of Satyam Traders, Indore and found that the Food Business Operator had various edible items stored for human consumption.
Samples of Shreedhi Ghee Agmark Special Grade 15 Kg. and Shreedhi Ghee (made from cow milk) Agmark Special Grade 15 Kg. were taken and sent for analysis.
In the analysis the samples were found to be substandard and of inferior quality.
Various other irregularities were also found.

3. Thereafter application under Section 68 of the Food and Safety NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:23956 2 WP-32494-2025 Standard Act was filed against the manufacturers of the spurious ghee.

sentences.text: During investigation notice was given to respondents 2 and 3 to establish the source of procuring the product.
Respondents 2 and 3 stated that they do not have any bill pertaining to purchase of the ghee from the petitioner.
During the course of proceedings the impugned notice has been issued to the petitioner.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that since respondents 2 and 3 have admitted that they do not have any bill of purchase of the ghee from the petitioner he could not have been impleaded as a party to the proceedings.
As per the investigation no invoice/cash memo was presented during investigation nor after its completion respondents 2 and 3 have stated that they procured the ghee from the petitioner.
Impleadment of the petitioner is hence illegal.
5. It is observed that the impugned notice dated 27.06.2025 only directs for the petitioner to appear on 04.07.2025.

The said date has already passed and it has not been stated by the learned counsel for the petitioner as to whether there was any representation on fact of the petitioner before the authority on that day.
Admittedly the petitioner is a manufacturer of the product which is alleged to be substandard and of inferior quality.
During the initial investigation bill was submitted by respondents 2 and 3 as regards purchase of the product from the petitioner company.
Though lateron they by their reply dated 08.11.2024 have contended that the same was due to a mistake by father of respondent No.2 but that would be a matter of adjudication.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:23956 3 WP-32494-2025 6.
There are two contradictory stands on record.

One where respondent No.2 states to have purchased the product from the petitioner company and the second where he states to have produced the bill due to having committed a mistake at the time of inspection.

That would be a matter of evidence but prima facie it appears to be a question which requires adjudication as to whether the product was purchased by respondents 2 and 3 directly from the petitioner or through some other hawker as contended by them.
Only on the basis of subsequent statements of respondents 2 and 3 the petitioner cannot be exonerated particularly at this stage when only notice for participation in the proceedings has been issued.

The order dated 27.02.2024 passed in M.Cr.C.
No.7719/2024 (Rahul Jain S/o Shri Anil Kumar Jain V/s. State of Madhya Pradesh) relied upon by the learned counsel for the petitioner is distinguishable on facts and does help him in any manner.

entities.text: Anil Kumar Jain V/s. State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Thus in view of the aforesaid, I am not inclined to interfere with the show cause notice issued to the petitioner.
The petition is hence found to be devoid of any merits and is hereby dismissed.
